Each link below was checked this session and loads.

- **[21 CFR 606.100 — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.100)**
  — the source for this module's central contrast: paragraph (c)'s first sentence (product-record
  review before release) versus its second sentence (the thorough, documented investigation of a
  discrepancy). Local verbatim copy: `sources/cfr/606.100.md`.

- **[21 CFR 11.10 — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/11.10)**
  — the full "Controls for closed systems" section this module's paragraph (j) comes from: written
  policies holding individuals accountable for actions taken under their electronic signatures.
  Local verbatim copy: `sources/cfr/11.10.md`.

- **[21 CFR 606.20 — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.20)**
  — the Personnel section behind this module's competence floor: paragraph (b)'s "adequate in
  number, educational background, training and experience" standard. Local verbatim copy:
  `sources/cfr/606.20.md`.

- **[AABB Quality Systems Framework (2021, public discussion draft PDF)](https://www.aabb.org/docs/default-source/default-document-library/standards/aabb-quality-systems-framework-2021.pdf?sfvrsn=a11081d1_2)**
  — AABB's own public description of the ten Quality System Essentials, including QSE 1
  (Organization) and QSE 2 (Resources), the two this module draws on for executive responsibility
  and competence. Use it to see the theme and scope of each QSE in AABB's own words; don't cite a
  standard number from it — see `sources/aabb/qse-framework.md` for why.

- **[Quality Assurance vs Quality Control / QA vs QC](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qu4Qz9rsryM)**
  (Pharmaguideline, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson: a short
  industry-education explainer on the QA versus QC distinction. Pharmaceutical-industry
  background, not FDA-issued and not blood-specific; use it for vocabulary, not for any
  regulatory claim. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA: Quality Systems Approach to Pharmaceutical Current Good Manufacturing Practice
  Regulations](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/quality-systems-approach-pharmaceutical-current-good-manufacturing-practice-regulations)**
  — FDA's own guidance page on the quality unit's role in a quality system. It is written for
  drug manufacturers (21 CFR Parts 210/211), not blood establishments, so read it as the
  regulator's clearest statement of what an independent quality unit is for, not as a rule that
  binds Lakeshore. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[ECA Academy: Responsibilities of Quality Assurance — FDA
  Perspective](https://www.gmp-compliance.org/gmp-news/responsibilities-of-quality-assurance-fda-perspective)**
  — a professional-association explainer on how FDA expects QA and QC duties to be divided and
  owned. Drug-GMP framing, but useful when you want to see the role split spelled out beyond
  this lesson's eight-item list. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Atlassian: RACI chart — what it is and how to use it](https://www.atlassian.com/work-management/project-management/raci-chart)**
  — a plain-language explainer of the responsible/accountable/consulted/informed framework the
  lesson's ITIL bridge leans on. Read it to sharpen the RACI vocabulary you already use, then
  apply it to the three signature boxes; it is general project management, not a quality-system
  source. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Cornell LII: 21 CFR Part 606 — Current Good Manufacturing Practice for Blood and Blood
  Components](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/part-606)** — the whole part that the
  lesson's 606.20, 606.100, and 606.160 citations come from, for browsing neighboring sections
  (for example, the organization and personnel provisions near 606.20) when a question goes
  beyond the quoted paragraphs. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

## Keep learning

Not official sources — good places to learn more about who owns what on a quality team.

- **[Responsibility assignment matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Responsibility_assignment_matrix)** (Wikipedia) — A neutral overview of RACI and its variants, including the common failure of tasks with no single accountable owner. Good for turning this lesson's ownership questions into a table you can hand your analyst. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Atlassian Team Playbook](https://www.atlassian.com/team-playbook)** (Atlassian, vendor) — A library of short team "plays" for clarifying roles and working agreements. Commercial content; use it for facilitation ideas, not as authority. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Review the ISC2 CISSP Certification Exam Outline](https://www.isc2.org/certifications/cissp/cissp-certification-exam-outline)** (ISC2) — The official CISSP outline; its Domain 1 (Security and Risk Management) covers governance, roles and accountability, a useful frame for who owns a control versus who operates it. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
